delta: residual after Stage2 — Stage1 PERF-7 (BLOCKING_IO sync fs) was marked HIGH but NOT fixed in Stage2 (`mcp-features/index.js` still imports readFileSync/writeFileSync)
issue: Sync fs (readFileSync/writeFileSync) still used in HTTP transport — every MCP tool call blocks the event loop, freezing ALL concurrent sessions on the same process
evidence: import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'fs' ... return JSON.parse(readFileSync(FEATURES_PATH, 'utf-8')) ... writeFileSync(FEATURES_PATH, JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) + '\n', 'utf-8')
estimated_impact: ~1-3ms block per call today (~10KB file). Under HTTP transport with N concurrent agent sessions, p99 grows linearly. Worst case (network FS / EBS stall): 50-200ms freeze of every active MCP session. In stdio mode impact is per-process so smaller, but Docker HTTP mode is the shared bottleneck.
recommendation: Switch to `fs/promises` readFile/writeFile + add 5s TTL in-memory cache mirroring `backend/utils/featureFlag.js`. Combine with PERF-D2 in one refactor.

delta: residual after Stage2 — Stage1 PERF-8 (MISSING_CACHE in MCP) still open; backend util has 5s TTL but MCP does not
issue: No in-memory cache parity with `backend/utils/featureFlag.js` — `readFeatures()` re-parses 10KB JSON on every tool call. LLM agent workflows commonly call get_feature_info / list_features 5-20x in a single run.
estimated_impact: Per call: ~0.3ms read + ~0.5-1ms JSON.parse for current file. In a 20-call agent loop = 20× redundant disk + parse work (~20-30ms wasted; small but pure waste). Scales linearly as features.json grows. Also misses an HTTP-mode multi-session amplification.
recommendation: Cache parsed JSON with 5s TTL + invalidate inside writeFeatures(). Mirror the exact mechanism used in `backend/utils/featureFlag.js` so the two layers stay consistent.

delta: NEW vs Stage1 — cache correctness/lost-update interaction Stage1 missed
issue: 5s TTL in-memory cache in `backend/utils/featureFlag.js` is per-process and has NO invalidation hook for writes coming from the MCP server. PATCH on the REST route invalidates the route-local cache (featureFlagRoutes.js line 19), but `isFeatureEnabled()` in controllers (separate cache in featureFlag.js) still serves stale flags for up to 5s after MCP/REST writes.
evidence: let cachedFlags = null; let cacheTimestamp = 0 ... if (cachedFlags && now - cacheTimestamp < CACHE_TTL_MS) { return cachedFlags } — no mtime check, no IPC/file-watch invalidation
estimated_impact: Not latency — correctness/UX. After an admin toggles a flag through AutoPilot/MCP, controllers using `isFeatureEnabled` keep serving the old value for up to 5s (and in worst case the two caches in the same Node process diverge from each other for 5s). At 100 req/s on `/api/products` with feature-gated branch, ~500 requests see stale state per toggle.
recommendation: Either (a) drop the cache and rely on OS page cache (file is 10KB — readFile is ~0.1ms anyway), or (b) add `fs.watch(FEATURES_PATH)` on module load to invalidate on mtime change, or (c) export and call `invalidateCache()` from PATCH route after rename. Option (c) is cheapest.

delta: NEW vs Stage1 — Stage1 only noted the read-modify-write race (RACE_CONDITION); did not analyse cold-cache spike
issue: Cache miss in `readFlags()` is not deduplicated — under traffic burst (e.g. SPA hard-refresh of a popular page), many concurrent requests after TTL expiry each re-read+parse features.json before any of them populates the cache.
evidence: if (cache.value && cache.expiresAt > now) { return cache.value } ... raw = await readFile(filePath, 'utf-8') ... cache = { value: parsed, expiresAt: now + CACHE_TTL_MS }
estimated_impact: At 100 RPS on `/api/featureflags` and 5s TTL, every 5s a brief spike of ~5-50 concurrent reads of the same 10KB file. Today negligible (~1ms each). Becomes ~10-50ms tail-latency event if file grows to 100KB+ or disk is slow.
recommendation: Add an in-flight promise dedup pattern: `let inflight; if (inflight) return inflight; inflight = readFile(...).finally(() => inflight = null)`. One read fans out to all waiters.

delta: residual after Stage2 — Stage1 noted `proshop-docs-index` scroll cost; Stage2 did not address it
issue: `proshop-docs-index` resource scrolls the entire Qdrant collection on every read with `limit=100` per page — many sequential round-trips for a list that only changes on re-ingest. No process-lifetime cache.
evidence: do { const response = await qdrant.scroll(COLLECTION, { limit: 100, offset, withPayload: ['source_file', 'type', 'last_modified'], withVector: false }); ... offset = response.next_page_offset } while (offset != null)
estimated_impact: Current corpus ~50 files → 1-2 round-trips (~30-50ms). At 500 chunks across 100 files = 5 round-trips (~150-250ms p95) per resource read. Cost is paid every time an agent enumerates resources at session start; in HTTP mode every new MCP session pays again.
recommendation: Cache the deduped list at process-lifetime in a module-level Map; invalidate only on tool error or via SIGHUP. Bump scroll `limit` to 1000 to reduce round-trips when cache must warm.

delta: residual after Stage2 — Stage1 PERF-17 (cache search queries) not implemented
issue: `search_project_docs` re-embeds every query via Cohere — no LRU. Agent workflows frequently re-ask near-identical questions across iterations; each pays ~150-400ms + Cohere API cost.
evidence: embedResponse = await cohere.embed({ texts: [query], model: 'embed-multilingual-v3.0', inputType: 'search_query', embeddingTypes: ['float'] })
estimated_impact: Per duplicate query: +150-400ms p95 and ~$0.0001 Cohere cost. In a multi-turn debugging session, 30-50% of queries are textual repeats. Also single point of failure: brief Cohere outage = tool errors that an LRU could mask.
recommendation: Add a process-local LRU (size 200) keyed by `sha256(query)` → vector, TTL ~1h. Also a fallback path: if Cohere times out and cache hit exists, serve cached vector.

delta: residual after Stage2 — Stage1 PERF-18 (getCollection per search) not implemented
issue: Every search runs `qdrant.getCollection(COLLECTION)` as a pre-flight health check before the actual search — adds a sequential Qdrant round-trip to every query.
evidence: try { await qdrant.getCollection(COLLECTION) } catch { collectionExists = false } ... results = await qdrant.search(COLLECTION, { vector, limit: top_k, withPayload: true })
estimated_impact: +5-20ms p95 per search (one full HTTP round-trip to Qdrant). On a fast local Docker Qdrant the impact is small; on a remote/managed Qdrant this becomes 30-80ms.
recommendation: Validate once at startup (main() already does it). On search, let `qdrant.search()` throw and convert NotFoundError into the COLLECTION_NOT_FOUND user-facing message in the catch.

delta: residual after Stage2 — Stage1 PERF-15 (unbounded chunks in memory) and PERF-16 (sequential batches) both open
issue: `buildChunks()` materialises every chunk from every md file into memory before the first embed call; then batches are processed strictly sequentially (no overlap of Cohere embed N+1 with Qdrant upsert N).
evidence: const chunks = buildChunks() ... for (let i = 0; i < chunks.length; i += BATCH_SIZE) { const batch = chunks.slice(i, i + BATCH_SIZE) ... await cohere.embed({ texts: batch.map(c => c.text), ... }) ... await qdrant.upsert(COLLECTION, { wait: true, points }) }
estimated_impact: Memory: today ~5MB heap for ~50 files; grows linearly. At 1000 docs × avg 5 chunks × 2KB = ~10MB — fine, but blocks until embed/upsert pipeline finishes if Cohere throttles. Wall-clock: sequential batches = N×(embed + upsert). 50 batches × (200ms+100ms) = ~15s; with parallelism-3 = ~5s. Ingest is rare so low severity.
recommendation: Two cheap wins: (a) turn `walkMd` into an async generator and pull one batch at a time; (b) use `p-limit(3)` over batches so embed of batch N+1 runs while upsert of batch N is in flight.

delta: residual after Stage2 — `idempotency cost` raised in Stage3 scope, NEW vs Stage1
issue: Full delete+recreate of the Qdrant collection on every ingest run — wipes payload index, forces full re-upsert even when only 1 file changed.
evidence: try { await qdrant.deleteCollection(COLLECTION) } catch { /* first run */ } await qdrant.createCollection(COLLECTION, { vectors: { size: VECTOR_SIZE, distance: 'Cosine' } })
estimated_impact: Wall-clock for a 1-file edit ingest = same as full ingest (~15s + Cohere $$). Disk write amplification. Negligible at current scale; flagging because docs/runbooks pipelines often run on every PR.
recommendation: Compute `sha256(text)` per chunk → use as Qdrant point id; only re-embed/upsert chunks whose hash changed (delete points whose source_file is no longer present). Keeps idempotency without nuking the whole collection.

delta: NEW vs Stage1 — autopilot proxy was not reviewed in Stage1
issue: `fetch()` to n8n webhook uses Node's default global agent with no keep-alive pool — every admin AutoPilot click opens a fresh TCP+TLS connection to (likely) a remote n8n instance.
evidence: upstream = await fetch(target, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...(apiKey ? { 'X-API-Key': apiKey } : {}) }, body: JSON.stringify(req.body || {}), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) })
estimated_impact: Per request: TLS handshake to remote n8n adds ~50-200ms p95 (RTT-bound). Today this is admin-only and low-frequency so impact is small UX latency; under any burst (e.g. AutoPilot rules firing) all calls pay the handshake. Also no per-request body size cap on the response — `await upstream.text()` could buffer a large unexpected response (DoS-of-self vector).
recommendation: Use a module-scoped `undici.Agent({ keepAliveTimeout: 30_000, keepAliveMaxTimeout: 60_000, connections: 10 })` and pass via `dispatcher`. Add `Content-Length` cap on the upstream response (e.g. reject > 64KB) — n8n responses are status-only.

delta: NEW vs Stage1 — frontend feature-flags layer was not reviewed in Stage1
issue: App mount dispatches `loadFeatureFlags()` once, with no retry/polling and no SWR. While load is in-flight, every `useFeatureEnabled(...)` returns `false` (initial state `flags=[]`) — feature-gated UI flashes the disabled branch then re-renders. Also no de-dup if two tabs/components dispatch concurrently.
evidence: useEffect(() => { dispatch(loadFeatureFlags()) }, [dispatch]) // App.js:33 ... const { data } = await axios.get('/api/featureflags') // featureFlagActions.js:15
estimated_impact: Visual jank / CLS risk: ~50-200ms window during which feature-gated screens render the OFF branch and then swap. For users on slow networks the window is longer (1-2s). Not a latency hit on the server, but a UX/perceived-perf issue. Also: no `Cache-Control` is set on `/api/featureflags` response (route returns raw JSON) → browser refetches on every navigation that mounts App fresh.
recommendation: Two complementary fixes: (a) on backend GET, send `Cache-Control: public, max-age=5, stale-while-revalidate=30` so browser short-circuits during navigation; (b) in `loadFeatureFlags`, return early if `getState().featureFlags.flags.length` and timestamp < 5s — prevents double-fetch under StrictMode/HMR. Optional: render a tiny skeleton/null for gated branches while `loading=true` to avoid the flash.

delta: NEW vs Stage1 — frontend hook was not reviewed in Stage1
issue: Two separate `useSelector` calls return new object references on every reducer dispatch unrelated to feature flags; combined with the `flags.find(...)` linear scan inside useMemo, every consumer re-evaluates on every flags-shaped state change. For 10 components calling the hook with 10 distinct keys, that's 100 array scans on every flags update.
evidence: const { flags } = useSelector((state) => state.featureFlags) ... return useMemo(() => { const flag = flags.find((f) => f.key === flagKey) ... }, [flags, flagKey, isAdmin])
estimated_impact: Today (~10 flags, ~5-10 hook consumers): ~50-100 array iterations per flags update — sub-millisecond, invisible. At 50 flags × 20 consumers = 1000 iterations per update — still <5ms but starts showing up as a render hitch on low-end devices. Also: `sessionStorage.getItem(TRAFFIC_KEY)` runs synchronously inside `useMemo` — every flag check is a sessionStorage round-trip (~10-50µs each).
recommendation: Two cheap wins: (a) memoise flags as a `Map<key, flag>` in the reducer (or via a selector with `reselect` `createSelector`) so lookup is O(1); (b) read the traffic bucket once at module scope (or in the App-level effect) and pass via Redux/Context, not via sessionStorage on every hook call.
